transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, Dora! Thanks for checking in. I do have a few questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's great! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense, thank you. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure about the specific instructions for your eye gel, I'd recommend checking with your GP or the pharmacist.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thanks. So, I'm very sensitive to bright light right now. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess this further. Do you have any redness or pain along with the light sensitivity?

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
No problem! Yes, it's quite common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time. 

However, if your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

How long has it been since your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been about a week now. Thank you for all your help, Dora. I don't have any more questions at the moment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great! So just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and don't hesitate to get in touch if you have any more questions about your recovery.
